headline: Discussed unreconciled town finances, audit delays, and a possible new Shepherd Glen School; approved July 9 minutes.
summary: The Commission discussed the delayed FY 2023–24 audit and incomplete bank reconciliations. Residents raised concerns about the Munis financial system and the Government Center exterior project. The only vote recorded was to approve the minutes from July 9, with 3 yes votes and 0 no votes.
decisions: Approved the minutes from July 9, 2026, by a roll call vote of 3 yes, 0 no, and 3 absent.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Finance Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, August 6, 2026 
  
 
Memorial Town Hall 
2372 Whitney Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner R. Scolnic at 6:03 PM. 
 
The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
 
Commissioner Rabbi Benjamin Scolnic, Chair 
Commissioner Michael Martin 
Commissioner Arnold Margolis 
 
Absent: 
Commissioner Myles Carter-Solomon, Youth 
Commissioner Bethany McCluster 
Commissioner Thomas Fortuna 
 
Also in attendance were Dr. Mario Ciccarini, Hamden Board of Education Member; Briana 
J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk; and 2 members of the public who 
attended in person, and 3 who attended online. 
2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Chairman R. Scolnic requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Thursday, July 9th, 
2026. 
 
The motion was made by A. Margolis and seconded by Commissioner M. Martin. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner R. Scolnic  
Commissioner A. Margolis 
Commissioner M. Martin 
 
No 
 
Absent 
Commissioner B. McCluster
Commissioner T. Fortuna 
Commissioner M. Carter-Solomon, Youth 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 3, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 3 
 
3. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION   
 Christopher Sherp, District 2, addressed the Commission regarding the status of the 
Town's financial audits and current financial reporting. He expressed concern that no 
completion date had been provided for the FY 2023–24 audit and suggested that the 
Commission speak with the Mayor regarding recent developments. He also discussed 
CBIZ, the Town's current auditor, and raised concerns regarding a potential conflict 
involving the Town's former auditing firm that could further delay completion of the audit. 
 
Mr. Sherp discussed the Town's financial management practices and compared them with 
the Board of Education's regular financial reporting. He also raised concerns regarding the 
Town's use of Munis, a Tyler Technologies financial management system, and whether the 
Town is fully utilizing the available modules and reporting capabilities. 
 
Alena Sherp, District 2, requested an update regarding the audit, noting that audit updates 
had been removed from the Legislative Council agenda and that residents have limited 
opportunities to obtain information regarding its status. 
 
Later in the discussion, Mrs. Sherp raised concerns regarding the Town's operating 
budget. She noted that the FY 2025–26 operating budget available online totaled 
approximately $313 million, while the FY 2026–27 budget was developed at approximately 
$304 million. She questioned how the Town would operate with the funding difference. 
 
Additional discussion included the Town's planned automated traffic enforcement cameras. 
It was noted that six cameras were anticipated, including red-light enforcement cameras, 
and concern was expressed that anticipated revenue had previously been incorporated 
into financial planning before the cameras were operational. 
 
Residents also discussed their ongoing efforts to raise financial concerns before the 
Legislative Council and expressed frustration with their ability to influence financial 
decisions. 
 
The Commission and residents additionally discussed the Town's use of Munis. It was 
noted that the Board of Education uses Munis for its financial reporting, while the Town has 
not fully utilized certain reporting and reconciliation functions. Discussion included a 
reconciliation module previously approved by the Legislative Council that, according to the 
discussion, had not yet been purchased or implemented. 
 
The EIFS exterior project at the Government Center was also discussed. The project 
involves replacement and improvement of portions of the building's exterior. It was stated 
that elevated moisture levels had been identified in portions of the building and were 
beginning to affect paper records stored near exterior walls. Concerns were also raised
regarding the potential for moisture to contribute to mold and affect employees working in 
the building. 
4. REPORT FROM EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS   
 
 
  1. Public Official or municipal employee representing the Mayor, designated by the 
Mayor.  
  No report was provided by a representative designated by the Mayor. 
  2. Representative of the Board of Education, designated by a majority vote of said 
Board  
  Board of Education Report 
 
Dr. Mario Ciccarini provided an update on behalf of the Board of Education. He stated 
that the Board generally does not hold regular meetings during the summer and that 
its last regular meeting was held in June. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini reported that positions had been eliminated as part of the budget 
process, while other positions had subsequently been posted as vacancies arose. 
 
The principal vacancy at Spring Glen School had been filled. Dr. M. Ciccarini also 
reported that Hamden High School Principal Eric Jackson resigned effective June 30, 
2026. Mr. E. Jackson had served as principal for approximately three years and was 
believed to be relocating to Florida. An assistant principal was expected to serve as 
interim principal. Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that he intended to seek clarification from the 
Superintendent regarding the decision to appoint an interim principal rather than 
immediately pursue a permanent appointment. 
 
Shepherd Glen School 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic revisited concerns previously discussed regarding the physical 
condition and long-term future of Shepherd Glen School. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that the Board of Education had discussed the possibility of 
engaging an architect or other professional to examine construction of a new school, 
but no formal planning process or committee had been established. He described the 
existing Shepherd Glen facility as significantly deteriorated and indicated that 
replacement may ultimately be more appropriate than continued renovation. 
 
Examples of school construction projects in Cheshire were discussed, including the 
replacement of Chapman School and construction associated with Norton School. 
 
The Commission discussed the logistics and financial implications of replacing 
Shepherd Glen. Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that a new school project could require 
approximately 5 to 7 years, from initial planning through completion. State 
reimbursement could cover a substantial portion of eligible construction costs; 
however, Hamden would remain responsible for the balance. Concern was expressed 
that the Town's current financial condition and bonding limitations could make 
financing its share of the costs difficult.
Commissioner A. Margolis noted that the existing Shepherd Glen property includes 
substantial land beyond the school's footprint and suggested that construction on the 
existing site could be explored. 
 
The Commission questioned which Legislative Council committee would have 
jurisdiction over long-range school facility planning and expressed concern that no 
committee or formal process currently appeared to be advancing the issue. 
 
Dr. M. Ciccarini stated that the Board of Education would resume its regular meeting 
schedule in September, with regular meetings held on the second Tuesday of the 
month. 
  3. Chair of the Legislative Council committee of jurisdiction over the budget or a 
member of said committee designated by the Chair.  
  No report was provided by the Chair of the Legislative Council Budget Committee or 
their designee. 
5. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE FINANCE COMMISSION CHAIR   
 Chairman R. Scolnic provided a recap of the Commission's previous meeting with Mayor A. 
Sendroff and Acting Finance Director Myron Hul. He stated that the discussion 
demonstrated that the Town's financial challenges extend beyond the delayed audit and 
include incomplete bank reconciliations. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic emphasized that reconciled financial records are fundamental to 
completing an accurate audit and determining the Town's actual financial position. He 
recalled asking at the previous meeting for the Town's current fund balance and stated that 
the Acting Finance Director was unable to provide an exact figure because the underlying 
financial records had not yet been fully reconciled. 
 
Commissioner A. Margolis explained that an audit requires complete reconciliations for the 
applicable fiscal year and that estimates used for budgeting may be within an expected 
range but cannot substitute for fully reconciled and audited figures. 
 
The Commission discussed the reasons the reconciliations had not been completed. 
Chairman R. Scolnic recalled that the Acting Finance Director attributed the backlog in part 
to understaffing within the Finance Department. Commissioners agreed that maintaining 
reconciled financial records is a fundamental responsibility regardless of other demands 
placed upon the department. 
 
Commissioner M. Martin noted that responsibility for the Town's financial management 
extended across multiple prior administrations and that the current Mayor inherited the 
responsibility for addressing longstanding deficiencies. Concern was expressed that, 
despite significant time and effort, the Town still lacks a complete picture of its financial 
condition. 
 
The Commission discussed the roles of CBIZ and CLA. CBIZ was identified as the Town's 
current independent auditor, while CLA was brought in to assist with reconciliation work 
and financial process analysis. Discussion indicated that multiple personnel from CLA and 
Town staff were working to resolve the outstanding financial records.
Chairman R. Scolnic discussed the possibility of greater State involvement in the Town's 
financial recovery. He noted that he had previously viewed the prospect of a State takeover 
negatively but questioned whether stronger external oversight might ultimately be 
necessary to implement the changes needed. 
 
The Commission discussed the value of a five-year financial plan and the need for a 
broader financial "reset." Chairman R. Scolnic asked what such a reset should include and 
emphasized the importance of establishing appropriate staffing, best practices, policies, 
procedures, and financial controls to ensure the Town does not revert to the same 
practices once the current backlog is resolved. 
 
Commissioner A. Margolis stated that CLA's work includes process analysis and that 
restructuring the Town's finance function would likely take considerably longer than one 
fiscal year. Discussion included reallocating resources, evaluating staffing levels and 
responsibilities, and determining the appropriate structure of the Finance Department. 
 
It was noted that the evaluation and implementation of recommended changes could 
require approximately 12 to 18 months, or longer, after the underlying issues are fully 
assessed. Commissioner Margolis emphasized that the Town's financial problems 
developed over several years and would therefore require substantial time to correct. 
 
Chairman R. Scolnic also reported continued discussions with the Mayor regarding 
potential task forces or working groups focused on long-range financial planning and 
expenditure reduction. Such groups could include representatives from the administration, 
Finance Commission, Legislative Council, and the public. The Chair stated that questions 
regarding legal requirements and staffing, including clerk support, were being reviewed. 
6. UPDATE REPORT FROM THE MUNICIPAL BOARD AND COMMISSIONS, INVITED 
GUEST   
 No additional reports were presented. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 The Commission did not enter Executive Session. 
8. REGULAR AGENDA   
 No regular agenda was presented. 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS   
 No unfinished business was presented. 
10. NEW BUSINESS   
 No new business was presented. 
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 Chairman R. Scolnic requested a motion to adjourn the meeting. 
 
Commissioner A. Margolis made a motion to adjourn the meeting, and the motion was 
seconded by Commissioner M. Martin.
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The Finance Commission's regular meeting adjourned at 7:00 pm.
